description: The Alberta Energy Regulator incidents page is the public information hub for pipeline incidents in Alberta, where pipelines carry raw oilfield production to processing facilities and finished petroleum products to market and the regulator oversees their design, construction, operation, discontinuation and abandonment under the Pipeline Act, the Pipeline Rules and Canadian Standards Association standards. It shows highlights on high consequence pipeline incidents and an interactive chart of pipeline incidents by consequence rating that can be drilled down through several levels, and points to the Compliance Dashboard where initial incident information is published and to the annual Pipeline Performance Report, which includes information on incidents starting in 2013. Coverage is the province of Alberta. Access: web dashboards and reports, with a Terms of Use link and a feedback form. Cost is free and no licence text was read. Caveats: summary counts and ratings, with detailed records in linked dashboards and reports, and initial incident information may be revised. It suits pipeline failure frequency and consequence estimates for oil and gas resilience studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
